Poll Vote & Share your view What is the most important measure to reduce the impact of sudden floods? Early warning systems Timely evacuation of residents Better disaster response and preparedness Stronger flood protection infrastructure 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Parts of West Bengal and Assam were placed on high alert after a glacial lake outburst in Bhutan triggered a flash flood, raising fears of a sudden rise in water levels along the Sankosh river. More than 10,000 people have been moved to relief shelters and safer locations in West Bengal, while authorities in Assam's Dhubri district have stepped up preparedness to deal with possible downstream effects.The outburst sent large volumes of water downstream through the Mo Chhu river towards the Sankosh river system, prompting authorities to activate disaster response mechanisms in vulnerable areas.The flood washed away infrastructure at the Gasa Tshachu natural hot springs in Bhutan's Gasa district. No injuries or loss of life have been reported, state broadcaster Bhutan Broadcasting Service (BBS) said on Friday.The full extent of the damage from the late-night flood remained unclear. BBS said the assessment was hampered by “darkness and the strong flow” of floodwaters. Two Bailey bridges, constructed using portable, prefabricated sections, may also have been washed away.According to Bhutan's national newspaper Kuensel, parts of the road leading to Laya village, where the hot springs are located, were washed away, making the route impassable.The road has been closed to traffic indefinitely. The area was evacuated before the floodwaters reached the hot springs.Authorities in West Bengal have alerted residents living along the Sankosh river and its tributaries following reports of the glacial lake outburst flood in Bhutan.Residents in the Darjeeling hills, Terai and Dooars regions have also been advised to remain alert and move to safer locations if they live in vulnerable areas.BJP MP from Darjeeling Raju Bista issued an alert through a post on X on Thursday, urging people living in the catchment areas of the Sankosh river and its connected tributaries to move to safer locations."A glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) has been reported at Lemthang in Bhutan. The overflowing water from the lake is flowing downwards through the Mofu River towards the Sunkosh River," the post read."Therefore, everyone living in the catchment areas of the Sunkosh River and all its connected tributaries have been informed to move to a safe distance immediately to protect their lives. Everyone in our Darjeeling hills, Terai and Dooars region are requested to stay alert," he added.State minister Nisith Pramanik said the government had received reports of the glacial lake outburst and that the overflowing water was moving towards the Sankosh river through the Mo Chhu river."Reports have just come in regarding a glacial lake outburst in Bhutan. Water from the lake is overflowing and flowing downstream into the Mo Chhu River, heading toward the Sankosh River. Residents living along the Sankosh River and its tributaries have been alerted; they are advised to move to a safe distance immediately to ensure their safety," Pramanik said.He said the water was expected to reach the plains within five to six hours, raising concerns about possible flooding."To manage the situation, the State Disaster Management Team has been activated, and the NDRF has also been notified. Disaster management volunteers have been instructed to be present on-site. The government is taking proactive measures and closely monitoring the situation to prevent any loss of life or property," he added.Alipurduar Superintendent of Police Amit Kumar Shaw appealed to residents not to panic, saying the administration was coordinating with Bhutanese authorities and disaster response agencies."First of all, I would like to tell the residents of the district that there is absolutely no need to panic. The situation is currently under control. We are in constant touch with the authorities in Bhutan. Our police team, the District Magistrate (DM) and the Block Development Officer (BDO) with their respective teams, along with all relevant agencies and stakeholders, are working together in close coordination," Shaw told ANI.He said the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) had been deployed in the area, while a National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) team was also on its way. Civil Defence personnel had additionally been mobilised to assist with preparedness measures."We have already moved approximately 4,000 to 5,000 people into shelters, utilising school buildings as relief centres. Additionally, more than 6,000 people have been relocated to safe areas," he said.Shaw said the intensity of the water flow had decreased slightly, according to the latest information received, but the administration remained on high alert."The police, the DM's office, and the BDO's office have made arrangements for dry food and drinking water. We have also ensured that other necessities, such as toilet facilities, are provided. We will wait to see what the situation looks like in two hours. We are fully prepared and ready to handle any emergency that may arise," he said.He added that a red alert was in force for the Sankosh river system and warned that the approaching floodwaters could carry dead fish and debris, including large pieces of wood and concrete."We expect to see water flowing through the Sankosh River, likely accompanied by dead fish, as well as large pieces of wood and concrete debris," Shaw said.Meanwhile, the Assam government said it was closely monitoring the situation following the glacial lake outburst in Bhutan, with Dhubri district placed on alert over possible downstream effects.The Sankosh river flows through Dhubri district, and authorities have stepped up vigilance amid the possibility of a sudden rise in water levels."The situation arising out of the Glacial Lake Outburst Flood in Bhutan is being closely monitored by HCM Dr @himantabiswa," the Chief Minister's Office said in a social media post."Team @dcofficedhubri is on ground and prepared to effectively deal with the downstream effects," it added.An Assam State Disaster Management Authority spokesperson said the water level of the Sankosh river was steady as of 6.30 am on Friday. The district administration and disaster response teams were on alert to tackle any eventuality.A special advisory issued by the ministry of Jal Shakti on Thursday for Assam and West Bengal said the Indian Embassy had reported a GLOF in Shintaphu Lake, located in Bhutan's Punatsangchhu river basin.Following reports of flash floods in the river's upper reaches, water levels in the Sankosh river could rise suddenly in Assam's Dhubri and West Bengal's Alipurduar districts, the advisory said.Local authorities in both districts were advised to remain alert, closely monitor the situation and take necessary precautionary measures.A glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF), also known as a jokulhlaup, occurs when the natural dam holding back a glacial lake fails or is breached, releasing large volumes of water downstream.Such floods can cause sudden destruction of roads, bridges, settlements and other infrastructure, particularly in mountainous regions.Shintaphu Lake, located below Wakila Mountain in Lungo, Laya Gewog, in Bhutan's Gasa district, is among 17 glacial lakes in the country identified as potentially dangerous, according to local reports.Gasa Tshachu, a popular natural hot spring in northern Bhutan, was also hit by a flash flood in 2021 when the Mochhu river changed course and swept through the area.The latest incident has renewed concerns over glacial lake outburst floods in the Himalayan region. In August, a flash flood near Nepal's border with China killed more than 1,500 people and left over 5,000 missing, according to the supplied report.
Article Summary: Glacial lake outburst in Bhutan raises fears of a sudden rise in water levels along the Sankosh river. More than 10,000 people have been moved to relief shelters and safer locations in West Bengal. Authorities in Assam's Dhubri district have stepped up preparedness to deal with possible downstream effects.

Article Title: Doctor's vacations at government medical colleges under Centre’s scanner
Article Text:
File photo: AIIMS Delhi

NEW DELHI: How much time do teaching doctors spend away from hospitals, and what happens to patient care and classes when they do? The Centre is seeking detailed records from three Delhi medical institutions as an expert panel reviews summer and winter vacations for govt medical colleges faculty.An expert committee constituted by Union health ministry to examine vacation and academic/on-duty leave arrangements for Central Health Service (CHS) teaching doctors had held its first meeting on Aug 31, according to official documents.The ministry sought information from Vardhman Mahavir Medical College and Safdarjung Hospital, ABVIMS and Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, and Lady Hardinge Medical College and its associated hospitals. A reminder issued on Sept 28 said the required information had not been received. On Oct 28, RML Hospital directed heads of clinical departments to submit verified data within two days.The prescribed format seeks details of faculty strength, the duration and actual dates of summer and winter vacations, the number of doctors allowed to take leave at a time, and the deployment of non-teaching doctors and residents during vacation periods.Institutions must also provide monthly data on outpatient attendance, admissions, ICU occupancy and surgeries for 2024-25 and 2025-26.The committee will assess whether the existing 50% faculty roster ensures uninterrupted patient care and whether vacations affect undergraduate and postgraduate teaching, examinations, research and academic administration.Sources alleged that some doctors combine vacations with academic leave and child care leave (CCL), extending their absence from work. One doctor was alleged to have taken academic leave nearly 100 times over the past 10 years, often for foreign visits. These allegations could not be established from the official documents and require documentary verification and a response from those concerned.Sources also questioned whether faculty in certain central govt medical colleges face vacation and administrative rules that are not applied in the same way at institutions such as AIIMS, PGI and UCMS. The extent of any differences in the applicable rules remains to be established.The ministry is also seeking details of outcomes from academic/on-duty leave, including research publications, grants, new projects, teaching initiatives and clinical skills acquired. Institutions have been asked whether doctors must submit reports after availing such leave and whether the outcomes are monitored.The documents do not announce any decision to reduce or cancel vacations. The committee is gathering data to assess the existing arrangements.
Article Summary: An expert committee constituted by Union health ministry to examine vacation and academic/on-duty leave arrangements for Central Health Service (CHS) teaching doctors. Ministry sought information from Vardhman Mahavir Medical College and Safdarjung Hospital, ABVIMS and Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital.

Article Title: Gadkari’s 140 kmph no-challan proposal faces legal, road safety hurdles
Article Text:
File photo:Nitin Gadkari

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Road transport minister Nitin Gadkari ’s recent announcement that he has asked authorities not to issue challans to cars travelling up to 20% above the prescribed speed limit on expressways — effectively allowing speeds of up to 140 kmph — cannot be implemented under the existing legal framework and may be detrimental to road safety , experts said.The announcement comes at a time when speeding remains the leading cause of road crashes and fatalities in India and globally. In India, more than 58% of road crash deaths (little over one lakh) in 2024 were attributed to speeding. Experts also pointed out that road infrastructure is not necessarily designed to safely accommodate cars travelling at 140 kmph.Speaking at a CII event on Tuesday, Gadkari said, “I was told that people are getting challans for speed violation on expressways for travelling little over 120 kmph. I have directed officers that no challans should be issued, if anyone is driving at speed that’s 20% more than 120 kmph. But if someone crosses that limit, issue challan.”Under the existing Motor Vehicles Rules, maximum permissible speed for cars on access-controlled expressways is 120 kmph. The limit is 100 kmph on four-lane roads and 70 kmph on other roads. The prescribed limits for other categories of vehicles are lower.The rules provide a limited relaxation for vehicles travelling up to 5% above the notified speed limit, beyond which the exemption from challans does not apply. This means the existing provision does not support a relaxation of 20% for cars on expressways.Moreover, state govts and other local authorities are empowered to prescribe lower speed limits on roads falling under their respective jurisdictions, taking into account local conditions and safety requirements.Experts said any nationwide relaxation would therefore need to be examined in the context of these existing provisions and powers of relevant authorities.They said allowing higher speeds could increase both likelihood of crashes and severity of injuries when collisions occur. They added that any move to relax speed limits must be backed by a legal framework and scientific assessment of road safety, rather than a general exemption from enforcement.
Article Summary: Road transport minister Nitin Gadkari has asked authorities not to issue challans to cars travelling up to 20% above the prescribed speed limit on expressways. The announcement comes at a time when speeding remains the leading cause of road crashes and fatalities in India and globally.

Article Title: NCLT, NCLAT hijacked by corporate affairs ministry: SC
Article Text:
SC slammed the corporate affairs ministry for "completely hijacking" NCLT and NCLAT, citing infrastructure failures, large vacancies and contractual hiring that undermine the tribunals' autonomy.

Contractual employees harassing judicial members, let past and present staff go: SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: In an outburst sure to embarrass the govt, Supreme Court Thursday slammed the ministry of corporate affairs for “completely hijacking” the two most important quasi-judicial financial adjudicatory bodies – National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) and the appellate NCLAT.The stinging remarks came from a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana while hearing petitioners who have been complaining for the last few months about the shoddy infrastructure, lack of support staff and large vacancies hampering the work in NCLT, which in the financial year 2024-25 had approved resolution plans worth Rs 55,000 crore. The tribunal adjudicates corporate civil disputes, company law violations and insolvency proceedings.“The system, the tribunals, we are compelled to observe, has been completely hijacked by the ministry of corporate affairs. That is the problem. And that is impinging on the autonomy of these institutions. These are the things we must look into. The ministry wants to have a complete whip over these tribunals. That is what is most unfortunate,” said the CJI.The bench has sought detailed proposals on infrastructure and staffing from the presidents of NCLT and NCLAT in four weeks.Appearing for NCLT Bar Association, senior advocate Sanjiv Sen said the roofs of certain floors in the building housing NCLT are collapsing and have become unusable. A large number of posts of judicial and technical members are lying vacant, he said, adding that the most unfortunate part is that out of 320 regular posts in NCLT, 253 are vacant.At this juncture, senior advocate Meenakshi Arora said the ministry has outsourced recruitment of contractual employees to a foreign firm and that could jeopardise the integrity of the important financial adjudicatory body. She said the existing contractual employees have already rendered service for eight years and must not be displaced.CJI Kant said, “We are not approving contractual recruitment of employees. It must be done through the Union Public Service Commission or Staff Selection Commission.” When Arora said termination of contractual employees must be stayed, the bench said, “We will not do any such thing at the behest of contractual staff. We would like to give full autonomy to the presidents of NCLT and NCLAT on this issue. The only thing is how soon it should happen. ”The CJI said, “Contractual employment means backdoor entry. In Bombay for instance, I know how these contractual employees ran away with original files and FIRs had to be registered. They do not care about the judicial members or technical members. Some technical members are still manipulating certain things.”“But these contractual employees are harassing the judicial members. So let the past and present contractual employees go. Let the autonomy of recruitment be with the president of the tribunals.... The heads of these tribunals are the most suitable persons to assist us in suggesting ways and means to smoothen and strengthen the day-to-day functioning of these two important tribunals, including requirements of land and buildings and safekeep of records. ”
Article Summary: SC slammed the corporate affairs ministry for "completely hijacking" NCLT and NCLAT, citing infrastructure failures, large vacancies and contractual hiring that undermine the tribunals' autonomy.Contractual employees harassing judicial members, let past and present staff go: SC.

Article Title: Introspect on Varanasi, Nagpur losses, Congress tells BJP
Article Text:
File photo: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh

NEW DELHI: A day after PM Narendra Modi’s sarcastic remark questioning the seats won by Congress in MLC polls, the party shot back that the PM should introspect why BJP lost in his constituency Varanasi, RSS headquarters of Nagpur, and other places.Congress spokesperson Jairam Ramesh said the MLC polls — in Varanasi, Nagpur, Lucknow, Prayagraj, and Patna — are a vote of no-confidence on Modi govt’s policies. Congress Maharashtra in-charge, Sirivella Prasad, said MVA won three of the five seats in the state, and the victory of Congress candidate in BJP stronghold of Nagpur “sends a strong message”.Ramesh said, “PM needs to introspect, but instead, he’s sermonising others. Before counting Congress’s seats, I wish he would also reflect on why BJP lost both seats in his own parliamentary constituency of Varanasi, and how Congress managed to defeat BJP in RSS’s stronghold of Nagpur?”Party chief Mallikarjun Kharge challenged Modi to dissolve Parliament and hold elections on ballot papers.
Article Summary: Congress spokesperson Jairam Ramesh said the MLC polls are a vote of no- confidence on Modi govt’s policies. Congress Maharashtra in-charge, Sirivella Prasad, said MVA won three of the five seats in the state.

Article Title: CCPA penalises Justdial, Sunrise Foods for safety, misleading product claims
Article Text:
File photo: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA)

NEW DELHI: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed penalties on online business directory Justdial and Sunrise Foods for violations involving consumer safety and misleading product claims.While it slapped a Rs 10 lakh penalty on Justdial for allowing listings of ammonium nitrate, a regulated explosive substance, on its platform without adequate safeguards, a Rs 1 lakh penalty was imposed on Sunrise Foods for marketing its bread as “100% Whole Wheat Bread” without disclosing its actual whole-wheat content.In an order on Wednesday, CCPA held that Justdial’s platform carried listings of ammonium nitrate without adequate disclosure of sellers’ valid licences issued by Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO), verification of buyers’ eligibility and mechanisms to ensure transaction traceability. The listings also lacked appropriate warnings about legal restrictions on the possession and use of the substance.Justdial argued that it was an online directory and information-listing service, not a trading platform and that the listings were old and sourced from public-domain information or user submissions. However, CCPA held that reliance on vendor representations and removal of listings only after complaints or regulatory intervention was insufficient.It directed the company to immediately discontinue listings, advertising and facilitation of access to the product.In a separate order, CCPA penalised Sunrise Foods for its “Everyday 100% Whole Wheat Bread”. The authority found the product contained only 64% whole wheat, below the prescribed 75% threshold for using the nomenclature “whole-wheat bread”. The packaging did not disclose the proportion of whole wheat, potentially misleading consumers about the product’s composition.Sunrise Foods argued that the “100%” claim referred to the wheat flour component being entirely whole-wheat flour rather than refined flour. However, CCPA said the representation created a misleading impression about the product’s composition. It directed the company to discontinue the claim across print, electronic and social media with immediate effect.It directed the company to immediately discontinue misleading advertisements across media and submit a compliance report within 15 days.
Article Summary: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed penalties on online business directory Justdial and Sunrise Foods. CCPA slapped a Rs 10 lakh penalty on Justdial for allowing listings of ammonium nitrate on its platform. A Rs 1 lakh penalty was imposed on Sunrise Foods for marketing its bread as “100% Whole Wheat Bread’

MUMBAI: For the atomic capital of India, Mumbai, it was a significant nuclear leap on Thursday.During the inauguration of the Indian Nuclear Society conference at HSNC University in Worli, Mumbai’s first School of Nuclear Science and Technology of the six-year-old university went “critical. ’’In layman’s parlance, going “critical’’ means it has started to function in phases.Speaking to TOI, university vice-chancellor Hemlata Bagla said that the new school will offer BSc and MSc courses and help in training professionals. It will go a long way in strengthening scientific foundation, opening new opportunities when there is a great deal of interest currently in the nuclear sector,’’ she stated.We already have a nuclear radiochemistry department at KC College which was established on October 10, 1997. Now we are going further into the radiochemistry department,’’ she said.The new school will collaborate with BARC, Department of Atomic Energy, Atomic Energy Regulatory Board and other nuclear establishments around the city.According to her, the school will also seek collaboration with global bodies like the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA).In his presidential address, former chairperson of Atomic Energy Commission, Anil Kakodkar, said that the 100 GW Nuclear Energy Mission was an ambitious one and right now it was only the beginning.We need to access energy which is three or four times more than what it is today to improve the quality of life and the only source is nuclear,’’ he told the large gathering of nuclear scientists, educationists and students gathered at the university.The former Indian nuke chief emphasised the important role played by uranium.He said that the Shanti Act passed in December 2025 allowed R&D, the development of different types of reactors like micro reactors and fusion reactors involving the participation of a large number of people.According to Kakodkar, for a smooth implementation of the Act, an intermediary agency has to be involved like the Indian Nuclear Society helping in important areas like capacity building and certification.
